idea.name: Funding carry (delta-neutral)
idea.blurb: Hyperliquid perps vs spot · collects funding · market-neutral
idea.source: Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov, 'Crypto Carry' (BIS WP 1087 / Management Science); Hyperliquid funding docs
idea.rule: Daily at 00:00 UTC: for coins whose 7-day average funding is above 15% a year (up to 6, richest first), buy spot and short the same amount of perp; keep while funding stays above 5%. Price moves cancel, the book earns the funding longs pay shorts.

backtest.caveat: Sharpe is flattered by the smooth hourly premium used as the basis proxy; real risks are tail events (short-squeeze margin calls, venue risk) and a yield that has been shrinking.

idea.name: Alt/BTC cross trend (market-neutral)
idea.blurb: Altcoins priced in BTC · trend-following · BTC-hedged, beta ~0
idea.source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen, 'Time series momentum' (JFE 2012); Menkhoff et al., 'Currency momentum strategies' (JFE 2012); Liu & Tsyvinski, 'Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency' (RFS 2021)
idea.rule: Daily at 00:00 UTC: for each altcoin, price it in BTC and average the trend sign over 10/20/42/84 days (-1..+1). Long the alt perp when its BTC cross trends up, short when it trends down, sized to 20% vol per cross / 21 alts; the BTC perp takes the opposite of the net alt exposure (market-neutral).

backtest.caveat: Weak edge: the direction calls beat random ones (p=0.03) but the Sharpe interval includes zero and the last two years were flat (Sharpe -0.06). On probation - it earns its place on paper or gets retired. Uses only ~36% of the book gross, so returns are small by design.

status.decider: Vol-managed crypto momentum v2 (market-neutral, bear-market guard)

idea.name: Vol-managed crypto momentum v2 (market-neutral, bear-market guard)
idea.blurb: Weekly winners minus losers · sized by momentum's own recent volatility
idea.source: Grobys, Kolari, Sandretto, Shahzad & Aijo, 'Cryptocurrency momentum has (not) its moments', Financial Markets and Portfolio Management 39(4) 2025; Barroso & Santa-Clara, 'Momentum has its moments', JFE 2015
idea.rule: Mondays 00:00 UTC: rank coins by 30-day return (skip the latest day); long the top fifth, short the bottom fifth, equal weight; scale the book by 20% / its own realised vol over the last 8 weeks (max 2x); v2: flat while the equal-weight coin index is down over the last 60 days.

backtest.caveat: On probation. The paper's key claim - that volatility scaling improves crypto momentum - did NOT replicate on our coins (scaled 0.51 vs unscaled 0.66). The winner/loser picks beat random ones only weakly (p=0.07), the Sharpe interval includes zero, and it lost money in 2025 and 2026. Backtest drawdown 42.5% would have tripped this book's 30% kill switch in 2025.

status.decider: Breakout Rocket v2: Donchian breakout ensemble (leveraged, BTC-regime gated)

idea.name: Breakout Rocket v2: Donchian breakout ensemble (leveraged, BTC-regime gated)
idea.blurb: Nine channel breakouts per coin · trailing stops · only while BTC is above its 100-day average · 80% vol, up to 4x
idea.source: Zarattini, Pagani & Barbon, 'Catching Crypto Trends; A Tactical Approach for Bitcoin and Altcoins', SSRN 5209907 (2025): Donchian ensemble over nine horizons, BTC net Sharpe 1.56, CAGR 30%, max DD 19% at a 25% vol target; top-20 rotation ~11%/yr alpha over BTC
idea.rule: Daily 00:00 UTC: for each coin run nine breakout systems (5-360 days): long on a close above the prior L-day high, out on a close below the trailing channel midpoint. Signal = share of systems long, counted only while BTC closes above its 100-day average (v2); size by 1/60-day vol; scale the book to 80%/yr vol, max 4x gross.

backtest.caveat: v2 (2026-10-07) adds a BTC 100-day-average gate: 50-125 days all helped, 150-200 hurt, so the gate works only while it is fast - a choice made with hindsight on one 6-year history. v1: Max risk by design: at this setting the backtest fell 82.5% peak-to-trough and lost 24.5% over the last 12 months (BTC -28.5%); returns stop growing above ~80-100% vol, so this is the top of the dial, not a step on the way up. The kill switch fires at -85%. Coins are today's Hyperliquid survivors, which flatters a long-only result. 0.83 correlated with Strategy 1. The long/short version did NOT replicate (Sharpe 0.78, short leg -12%/yr), so it is long-only.

idea.name: 52-week-high momentum (market-neutral)
idea.blurb: Long the coins pinned near their yearly high · short the ones far below it
idea.source: George & Hwang, 'The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing', Journal of Finance 59(5) 2004; Ficura, 'Impact of size and volume on cryptocurrency momentum and reversal', Prague University of Economics and Business WP 2023/5
idea.rule: Mondays 00:00 UTC: PTH = last close / 52-week high for coins with a full year of data; long the top 30% by PTH, short the bottom 30%, equal weight, 0.5x equity per side.

backtest.caveat: Picks beat random coin picks (p=0.02) and ranking by the 52-week high beats ranking by the 52-week return (-0.13), as the paper predicts, and it hedges Strategy 1 (corr -0.42). But the Sharpe interval includes zero, the walk-forward that re-picks the lookback each quarter made only 0.22, it leans short the market (corr -0.51 with the equal-weight basket), and funding before Oct 2024 is missing from the history.

status.decider: Winners vs Bitcoin v2 (alt momentum, BTC-hedged, bear-market guard)

idea.name: Winners vs Bitcoin v2 (alt momentum, BTC-hedged, bear-market guard)
idea.blurb: Buys the strongest alts · shorts only Bitcoin as the hedge · an alt-season catcher (probation)
idea.source: Fieberg, Liedtke & Zaremba, 'Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints', International Review of Financial Analysis 94 (2024); Grobys, Kolari, Sandretto, Shahzad & Aijo, 'Cryptocurrency momentum has (not) its moments', Financial Markets and Portfolio Management 39(4) 2025
idea.rule: Mondays 00:00 UTC: buy the 30% of altcoins with the best 28-day return (equal weight, 1x equity) and short BTC perp for their combined 90-day beta to BTC. Never shorts an altcoin. v2: flat while the equal-weight coin index is down over the last 60 days.

backtest.risk_dial: 1x live; 1.5x is the top of the growth curve (42.5%/yr) but max DD 80%
backtest.caveat: Probation, and the numbers say why: the whole edge is the 2021 alt season (+1,269%). Without 2021 the Sharpe is -0.02, the walk-forward made 0.13, and random alt picks with the same BTC hedge already score 0.47 (p=0.057 vs placebo). It is on paper as a cheap, market-neutral-on-paper 'alt-season option' that diversifies Strategy 8 (corr -0.27): it bleeds slowly while Bitcoin leads and pays off big when alts run. The BTC hedge does not remove alt-crash risk (60.7% max DD).

status.decider: Coin Rider v2: rotates into the next breakout

idea.name: Coin Rider v2: rotates into the next breakout
idea.blurb: Rides the dev-vetted Solana/Base/Robinhood-chain coin breaking out hardest · checked hourly · sells when it stops making new highs for 24h or falls 2 vols, then jumps to the next breakout (v2, probation)
idea.source: Zarattini, Pagani & Barbon, 'Catching Crypto Trends; A Tactical Approach for Bitcoin and Altcoins' (SSRN 5209907, 2025); Bui & Nguyen, 'Systematic Trend-Following with Adaptive Portfolio Construction' (arXiv 2602.11708, 2026); Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu, 'Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency', Journal of Finance 77(2) 2022; dev screen per Trockman, van Tonder & Vasilescu (MSR 2019)
idea.rule: Hourly: if flat, buy (1x) the dev-vetted coin that just closed at a new 7-day high with the best 28-day risk-adjusted return. Sell when it closes 2 daily vols below its peak OR makes no new high for 24h; bar it 24h and buy the next breakout in the same hour.

backtest.plain_hourly_hop_to_hottest_coin: lost 55-99.9% on both histories (the hottest coin lags the next hour)
backtest.caveat: v1 rode one coin until a ~30% trailing stop, so it could sit on a drifting coin for days (it held PUMP from Oct 5). v2 sells a ride that has not made a new high for 24h and rotates into the next breakout, and uses a 2-vol stop. It beat v1 in both histories (1h 1.85 vs 0.98; 4h 0.68 vs 0.14, drawdown 65% vs 94%), but the stale/stop setting was picked from a 24-cell grid, picking a random breakout does as well as the strongest one (the edge is breakout + fast exits), and 2026 on 4h bars is still -26%. Hopping every hour to the hottest coin was tested and loses money. One coin at a time: expect 40-65% drawdowns; kill switch at 60%.

scene.title: Coin Rider - one coin at a time
scene.subtitle: bars = each coin's 28-day risk-adjusted momentum (last 30 days); the gold ribbon is the coin being ridden

idea.name: Breakaway Alts (coin-specific jump drift, BTC-hedged)
idea.blurb: Buys an alt the day it jumps on its own news · hedges out Bitcoin · rides the 5-day drift · 2.5x
idea.source: Liu & Tsyvinski, 'Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency', Review of Financial Studies 34(6) 2021 (crypto underreacts: momentum and attention effects at 1-4 weeks); Caporale & Plastun, 'Momentum effects in the cryptocurrency market after one-day abnormal returns', Financial Markets and Portfolio Management 34 (2020); Grobys et al., 'Cryptocurrency momentum has (not) its moments', FMPM 39(4) 2025
idea.rule: Daily 00:00 UTC: residual = alt return - 90d beta x BTC return; if yesterday's residual > 2.5 sd of its 90-day history, hold the alt for 5 days (20% equity each, max 1x), short BTC for the beta, whole book 2.5x. Never shorts an alt.

backtest.caveat: Strong and stable for a crypto anomaly: positive every year, every threshold/hold cell (Sharpe 0.66-1.45), 3x costs and a day-late entry. But random alts bought on the same days already make Sharpe 0.71 (the days themselves are alt-friendly), so the coin choice adds about 0.5; the walk-forward made 0.87, not 1.22. At 2.5x the backtest lost 67% peak to trough and a worst day of -30% (kill switch at 75%). Pre-2023 prices partly predate Hyperliquid listings.

scene.title: Breakaway Alts: coin-specific jumps and the drift that follows

status.decider: Volume Spotlight (high-volume return premium, BTC-hedged) - probation

idea.name: Volume Spotlight (high-volume return premium, BTC-hedged) - probation
idea.blurb: Buys alts trading 2x+ their normal volume · hedges out Bitcoin · holds a week · 1.25x · on probation
idea.source: Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin, 'The High-Volume Return Premium', Journal of Finance 56(3) 2001; Liu & Tsyvinski, 'Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency', Review of Financial Studies 34(6) 2021 (attention shocks); counter-evidence: Garfinkel, Hsiao & Hu, Financial Management 54(3) 2025
idea.rule: Daily 00:00 UTC: AV = yesterday's dollar volume / prior-30-day average; alts in the top 20% by AV with AV > 2 are held 7 days (20% equity each, max 1x), BTC short for their 90d betas, whole book 1.25x. Never shorts an alt.

backtest.caveat: PROBATION - did not pass the lab bar: Sharpe CI includes zero, deflated Sharpe 0.19, the second half of the sample made Sharpe 0.10 and 2025 lost 44% at 1.25x. In its favour: volume-picked coins beat random alts bought on the same days (p = 0.002) and buying quiet coins loses. It overlaps Strategies 9 and 11 (corr 0.73 / 0.66): most of the edge comes from spotlight days that were also up days. Volume history only from 2023 (Hyperliquid candles).

scene.title: Volume Spotlight: abnormal volume and the week that follows

idea.name: EMA-800 Trend (freqtrade strategy from GitHub, 2x)
idea.blurb: Open-source freqtrade strategy, unchanged: long each coin that crosses above its 800-hour EMA · out 1% below it or 15% off the peak · checked hourly · 2x
idea.source: Paul Csapak, EMAPriceCrossoverWithThreshold.py, github.com/paulcpk/freqtrade-strategies-that-work (README: +118.5% on 1h bars, Mar 2018 - Mar 2020); screened against freqtrade/freqtrade-strategies Supertrend.py (rejected)
idea.rule: Hourly, per coin: buy when the 1h close crosses above its 800-bar EMA; sell below 0.99 x EMA800 or 15% under the highest close since entry. Each open coin holds 2/N of equity (N = 22).

backtest.period: 1h Apr-Oct 2026 (how it trades); 4h with EMA200 (= 800h) Jul 2024-Oct 2026
backtest.risk_dial: 4h (2.3 years): 1x 19.9%/yr DD 41% · 1.5x 25.7%/yr DD 57% · 2x 28.0%/yr DD 70% (live, top of the growth curve) · 3x 21.5%/yr DD 87%
backtest.caveat: A published, unmodified open-source rule, so nothing was fitted here, and it beats random entries (p=0.024 hourly, 0.048 on 4h). But it is classic slow trend-following: 0.93 correlated with Strategy 1, so it adds leverage to the same bet more than a new edge. On 2024-2026 4h bars it made 48.9% at 1x while holding everything lost 3.7%, yet lost 15.8% in 2025; at the live 2x the backtest drawdown is 70% (kill switch 75%). The official freqtrade Supertrend strategy, screened first, failed (4h: -69%).

idea.name: Roll-Off Echo (trade the 24h-change display)
idea.blurb: When yesterday's big 4h move drops out of the '24h change', the market echoes it · 4h trades · 3x
idea.source: Fracassi, 'Pure Momentum in Cryptocurrency Markets', Fields Institute seminar (Feb 2023): investors react to changes in the reported 24-hour return that carry no information; Liu & Tsyvinski, 'Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency', RFS 34(6) 2021 (attention drives crypto returns)
idea.rule: Every 4h (UTC grid): z = market 4h return of the bar 20-24h ago / std of the 42 market 4h returns ending with it; if |z| > 2 hold all coins equal-weight against that bar's sign for 4h, else flat; 3x.

backtest.caveat: Probation. The mechanism shows up only at the exact 24h lag (every other lag loses) and beats random timing (p=0.006), but the money is thin and lumpy: 2x costs leave Sharpe 0.07, dropping the 5 best days leaves 0.02, the walk-forward threshold choice lost (-0.21), 2025 lost 5.7% at 1x and most of the profit is buying after yesterday's crash rolls off (+41 bp/trade; shorts +4 bp). Only 2.3 years of 4h data; the source is a seminar talk, not a published paper. At 3x a single 4h bar lost 15.7%; kill switch at 80%.

scene.title: Roll-Off Echo: big 4h moves from yesterday leave the 24h window - trade the echo

status.decider: MACD Rank: top 5 vs bottom 5 coins by trend score (desk-built)

idea.name: MACD Rank: top 5 vs bottom 5 coins by trend score (desk-built)
idea.blurb: Long the 5 coins with the strongest 2-3 week trend, short the 5 weakest · daily · 1x · built and attacked by the research desk (paper probation)
idea.source: Research-desk framework (scan, hypotheses with a named loser, gates, risk officer, paper) applied to its own worked example: 'combine short-term momentum and price-normalized MACD, long the top 5, short the bottom 5, rebalance daily'; crypto under-reaction: Liu & Tsyvinski, Review of Financial Studies 2021
idea.rule: Daily 00:00 UTC: score = z(14-day return) + z(MACD(12,26)/price) across coins; long the top 5 (10% each), short the bottom 5 (10% each). A short up 50% from entry is closed. Kill switch at -15%.
idea.status: live paper (probation: failed the quality gate under adverse funding)

backtest.placebo_note: random picks held 9 days (turnover-matched): mean -0.53, p95 0.09
backtest.plateau: 15 cells (look 7-28 x k 3/5/7): min 0.65, median 1.19, 73% above 1
backtest.gates: scorecard (scripts/gate_check.py): PAPER with funding as recorded; BACK TO RESEARCH under the risk officer's adverse funding proxy (Sharpe 0.91 < 1, below holding everything 1.06). Risk officer: KEEP for paper only. Rejected today: H1 vol-squeeze breakout (Sharpe -0.54), H2b BTC-hedged variant (KILL: 2021 makes the curve), H3 negative-funding squeeze (-0.02).
backtest.caveat: Funding history starts Oct 2024; charging the long leg 30%/yr before that drops the Sharpe to 0.91. Without its 10 best days the Sharpe is 0.49, the top 5 coins make half the profit, the short leg loses (-32%/yr) and works as a costly hedge, and the trailing year is weak (0.38). Paper pass mark (risk officer): 90 days, net Sharpe >= 0.5, positive without the 3 best days, realised costs < 2x model, drawdown < 15%, 60-day correlation with S4/S5 < 0.6.

ideas.verdict: Restarted on a fresh $10k: v1 won 70% of trips but lost 2c/contract to adverse queue fills and taker bail-outs (maker exits +$41, taker -$251 in the last 60).

ideas.name: Breakout Rocket v2: BTC 100-day trend gate - Strategy 6
ideas.rule: Breakout signals count only while BTC closes above its 100-day average.

ideas.name: Vol-managed momentum v2: bear-market guard - Strategy 5
ideas.rule: Flat on weeks that start with the equal-weight coin index down over the last 60 days.

ideas.name: Winners vs Bitcoin v2: bear-market guard - Strategy 9
ideas.rule: Flat on days the equal-weight coin index is down over the last 60 days.

ideas.name: Volatility-squeeze breakout, 4h, long/short (desk H1)
ideas.rule: 4h close beyond the previous 20-bar range while ATR(14) < its 100-bar average; stop 2 ATR, target 3 ATR, 60-bar max hold.
ideas.verdict: Rejected: 2,597 trades, Sharpe -0.54, PF 0.98 Jul 2024-Oct 2026; longs lose, shorts barely positive.

ideas.name: Negative-funding squeeze (desk H3)
ideas.rule: Long the 3-5 coins with the lowest 3-day funding (or all negative-funding coins), short BTC for the same notional.

ideas.name: MACD Rank long top 5 vs BTC (desk H2b)
ideas.rule: Long the top 5 by z(14d return)+z(MACD/price), short BTC for the same notional.
ideas.verdict: Rejected by the risk officer: Sharpe 1.23 but 2021 +1,648% makes the curve, trailing year 0.06, corr 0.69 with S9.

ideas.name: MACD Rank: top 5 vs bottom 5 by trend score - Strategy 16
ideas.source: research-desk framework worked example; Liu & Tsyvinski RFS 2021
ideas.rule: Daily: score = z(14-day return) + z(MACD(12,26)/price); long top 5, short bottom 5, 10% each, 1x; short stop +50%; kill -15%.
ideas.verdict: Paper probation: Sharpe 1.21 (0.91 with an adverse 30% funding proxy), 40.8%/yr, DD 42.7% Nov 2020-Oct 2026, turnover-matched placebo p=0.005, walk-forward 0.99; fails the desk's Sharpe>1/benchmark lines under adverse funding; risk officer KEEP for paper only.
